partial_evaluations.label: baseline peak on official distribution
partial_evaluations.selection: checkpoint-100352 has the highest training-window success proxy of all 24 saved candidates (0.97 versus 0.93-0.95 for every later checkpoint) but that proxy is measured only on the 14-20 cm training range. Measuring it on the official 6-20 cm distribution with the emitted per-episode diagnostics (target_radius_cm, min_distance_cm, first_reach_step, max_held_steps, hold_interruptions) shows whether the near-objective proxy survives the radius shift and whether failures concentrate on radii below 14 cm or in hold maintenance. This decides whether the next experiment can be a targeted near-range curriculum or must address a structural reach/hold deficiency.

partial_evaluations.label: baseline final on official distribution
partial_evaluations.selection: The final saved checkpoint carries a lower training-window proxy (0.95) than checkpoint-100352 (0.97), and the training-window proxy declined after 100k (0.93-0.95 through 120832), so the training-time ordering of the two leading checkpoints is ambiguous and the proxy conflates the 14-20 cm range. Measuring it on the same 200 official-distribution episodes (same seed) as checkpoint-100352 supplies a paired, reduced-variance comparison of the two leading checkpoints on the actual task. This decides which checkpoint is designated as the working lineage and therefore which weights a continuation would extend.
